q-163236.name: Question 1
q-163236.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$
q-163236.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 3=3.
$$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{x}^{2}y+{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+x]_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}+3) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that

Area(D)=1⋅3=3.

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

fave=1Area(D)∬Df(x,y)dA=13∬D(x2+3y2)dA=13∫03∫01(x2+3y2)dydx=13∫03[x2y+y3]y=0y=1dx=13∫03(x2+1)dx=13[x33+x]x=0x=3=13(333+3)=4.

q-163241.name: Question 2
q-163241.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=x+3{y}^{2}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,x\le y\le x+1\}$ given that the area of the region is $2.$
q-163241.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{∬}_{D}x+3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x}^{x+1}x+3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[xy+{y}^{3}]_{y=x}^{y=x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[3{x}^{2}+4x+1]\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+x]_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(18-0) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

q-163255.name: Question 3
q-163255.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=12x{y}^{3}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \frac{x}{4}\}$ given that the area of the region is $\frac{1}{2}.$
q-163255.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}{∬}_{D}12x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x/4}12x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}[3x{y}^{4}]_{y=0}^{y=x/4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3{x}^{5}}{256}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2[\frac{{x}^{6}}{512}]_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{8}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-163256.name: Question 4
q-163256.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)={e}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ on the disk of radius $\frac{1}{2}$ centered at the origin.
q-163256.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \frac{1}{2},\,0\le \theta <2\pi \}.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{{r}^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{[\frac{{e}^{{r}^{2}}}{2}]}_{0}^{1/2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(\frac{{e}^{1/4}}{2}-\frac{1}{2})\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[4]{e}-1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[4]{e}-1}{2}[\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[4]{e}-1}{2}(2\pi -0) \\  & =(\sqrt[4]{e}-1)\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{4}{\pi }\cdot (\sqrt[4]{e}-1)\pi =4(\sqrt[4]{e}-1).
$$

Question 4
?

Find the average value of the function f(x,y)=ex2+y2 on the disk of radius 12 centered at the origin.

a
4(e2−1)
b
4(e4−1)
c
2(e4+1)
d
e8−2
e
2(e2+2)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

Area(D)=π⋅(12)2=π4.

The average value of the function over a region D is given by

fave=1Area(D)∬Df(x,y)dA.

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∬Df(x,y) dA=∬Δ f(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ)r drdθ.

In polar coordinates (r,θ), the region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ):0≤r≤12,0≤θ<2π}.

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∬Dex2+y2dA=∬Δe(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2rdrdθ=∬Δer2rdrdθ=∫02π[er22]01/2dθ=∫02π(e1/42−12)dθ=e4−12∫02πdθ=e4−12[θ]02π=e4−12(2π−0)=(e4−1)π.

Therefore,

fave=4π⋅(e4−1)π=4(e4−1).

q-163277.name: Question 5
q-163277.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14285580/assets/06a853735916ae3219eea02fa7e7e30d9e941106600cd5b642d951f553aace59.png)

Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=5y({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})$ on the semicircle shown above.
q-163277.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Notice that the region $D$ represents a portion of the disk of radius $1$ centered at 
$(1,0).$

Cartesian and polar coordinates are connected by the following equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

With that is mind, let's now write the $y=-\sqrt{2x-{x}^{2}}$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\sqrt{2x-{x}^{2}} \\ {y}^{2} & =2x-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2x \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2}-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

Therefore, in polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le 0\}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}5y({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}5r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ((r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }5{r}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }5{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta [{r}^{5}]_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ((2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{5}-0)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =32{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{5}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =32{[-\frac{1}{6}{cos}^{6}⁡\theta ]}_{-\pi /2}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{16}{3}[{cos}^{6}⁡(0)-{cos}^{6}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =-\frac{16}{3}(1-0) \\  & =-\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}\cdot (-\frac{16}{3})=-\frac{32}{3\pi }.
$$

Question 5
?

Find the average value of the function f(x,y)=5y(x2+y2) on the semicircle shown above.

a
−323π
b
−165π
c
−83
d
−323
e
−163π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

Area(D)=12⋅π⋅12=π2.

The average value of the function over a region D is given by

fave=1Area(D)∬Df(x,y)dA.

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∬Df(x,y) dA=∬Δ f(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ)r drdθ.

Notice that the region D represents a portion of the disk of radius 1 centered at (1,0).

Cartesian and polar coordinates are connected by the following equations:

{x=rcos⁡θy=rsin⁡θ

With that is mind, let's now write the y=−2x−x2 in polar coordinates:

y=−2x−x2y2=2x−x2x2+y2=2x(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2=2rcos⁡θr2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=2rcos⁡θr2=2rcos⁡θr2−2rcos⁡θ=0r(r−2cos⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have r=2cos⁡θ.

Therefore, in polar coordinates (r,θ), the region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ):0≤r≤2cos⁡θ,−π2≤θ≤0}.

Therefore, we obtain

∬D5y(x2+y2)dA=∬Δ5rsin⁡θ((rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2)rdrdθ=∫−π/20∫02cos⁡θ5r4sin⁡θ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)drdθ=∫−π/20sin⁡θ∫02cos⁡θ5r4drdθ=∫−π/20sin⁡θ[r5]02cos⁡θdθ=∫−π/20sin⁡θ((2cos⁡θ)5−0)dθ=32∫−π/20sin⁡θcos5⁡θdθ=32[−16cos6⁡θ]−π/20=−163[cos6⁡(0)−cos6⁡(−π2)]=−163(1−0)=−163.

Therefore,

fave=1(π2)⋅(−163)=−323π.
